rationale: Pins C++ calls, instantiates (new-expression), imports (include dependency) and references (using dependency), plus the imports payload, for the completeness gate Section B; mirrors the c/c-completeness fixture for the systems family. M14 ONTOLOGY (2026-10-04): `#include` is C++'s FILE INCLUSION and is now a first-class `imports` edge — the same kind, with the same metadata, the C lane already emits for the identical construct (pinned there by c/macro-composed-include, reverted there by the `c/include-kind-downgraded` mutant). The measured reason: the one consumer that answers "what does this module depend on" is the LSP usages file-level section, which filters on `relationship_type IN ('imports','exports')` (src/lsp/graph_request.ts, src/lsp/graph_usages.ts), so a C++ include was invisible to it no matter what its metadata said. A LABEL move, not an edge move — 5,404 include sites in 905 corpus files, 5,118 distinct module names, and the include-dependency row count is identical before and after. The `using`-dependency rows stay `references`: an include dependency and a using-dependency are two facts, and only the first is file inclusion.

forbidRelationships.note: #910-for-cpp: the include dependency carried as `references` + metadata.isImport. Forbidding the OLD label is what makes this a regression gate for a downgrade rather than a note about one — the same discipline c/macro-composed-include uses, and the reason a silent relabel cannot pass.
